title: How cost is built
summary: Sum of per-line costs, control structures, and dependence on n. Step-by-step tracing and execution counts give evidence; asymptotic conclusions remain yours to justify.

learningObjectives.text: Build T(n) as a sum of contributions per line or block using how many times each part runs.
Recognize that citing asymptotic notation without counting evidence is not a complete analysis.

sections.title: Sum of costs and control structures

content.text: A standard approach assigns a cost to each line (or block) and multiplies by how many times it runs. Control structures decide repetitions: an
chooses branches; a loop repeats its body according to the guard.

blocks.title: Saying O(n) is not enough—you must justify it

content.text: Notation summarizes growth, but analysis explains where it comes from: which lines dominate, how often they run, and why. AALIE shows executions and counts so you can tie evidence to your argument; copying the final label without the count leaves the analysis incomplete.

In many pedagogical models the loop condition is evaluated one more time than the body runs: when the condition fails, the body no longer runs but the check still does. That convention explains small differences between how often you see the header and the body in a trace. Use it to align manual counting with what the tool shows.

Step-by-step tracing shows the order lines and conditions are visited. Per-line execution counts summarize how much each part contributed. Together they let you verify hypotheses (e.g. body runs n times and exit check runs once more).
